findings.title: Privileged value exposed through public env prefix
findings.description: A sensitive value bound to public env name NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL may be exposed to client bundles.

evidence.summary: Public prefix binding NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL correlates with sensitive material.

findings.impact: Client-exposed privileged values can be recovered from built assets or browser contexts.
findings.remediation: Remove privileged values from public env prefixes. Keep secrets on the server and rotate exposed credentials.
limitations: This finding confirms repository evidence of a public-prefix binding with sensitive material, not a deployed bundle contents dump.

findings.title: Sensitive value in a Git-tracked env file
findings.description: Sensitive material was observed in a Git-tracked environment file.

evidence.summary: A sensitive value was present in a tracked .env file.

findings.impact: Tracked env files can expose secrets to anyone with repository access and to CI clones.
findings.remediation: Remove secrets from tracked env files, rotate them, and keep only non-secret templates such as placeholders in examples.
limitations: This finding confirms repository evidence only and does not validate remote credential acceptance.

findings.title: Table created without observable RLS enablement or policy
findings.description: Table public.passwordresettoken is created in migrations without an observed ENABLE RLS or policy.

evidence.summary: CREATE TABLE was observed without a correlating ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY or CREATE POLICY in the scanned migrations.

findings.impact: If the deployed database also lacks RLS/policies, privileged API roles may read or write broader row sets than intended.
findings.remediation: Confirm production RLS and policies for this table. Prefer enabling RLS and adding explicit policies in migrations.
limitations: Absence of local RLS/policy evidence must not be interpreted as proof that production RLS is disabled.
Only scanned migration-like SQL files were considered.
